annotation.title_clean: Liability for robots II: an economic analysis
annotation.title_en: Liability for robots II: an economic analysis
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Guerra, A.; Parisi, F.; Pi, D.
annotation.summary_en: Economic-model paper proposing a 'manufacturer residual liability' rule for robot accidents: operators and victims are liable for negligence, while manufacturers bear residual strict liability for non-negligent accidents. It argues this yields efficient care, activity levels, R&D investment in safer robots, and adoption of safer technology.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes manufacturer residual liability (MRL) for robots operated with human intervention.
Operators and victims are liable for negligent accidents; manufacturers are residually liable otherwise.
MRL incentivizes manufacturer R&D into safer robots, lowering prices and driving out unsafe technology.
Existing negligence and products liability rules inadequately align incentives for robot accidents.
Compensation goes to victims, unlike Shavell's decoupling proposal where damages are paid to the state.
